comparable_reason: pe_h0 is pinned to its own ceiling by construction and is therefore nearly constant across models. Its bar count is m = N-1 for a cloud of N mean-pooled sentence representations, so PE saturates at log2(N-1): on iid Gaussian clouds I measure PE/log2(m) = 0.999599 / 0.999937 / 0.999970 at N = 20 for D = 64/256/1024, and 0.99939-0.99998 across N = 20/50/100/200/400 -- the value carries essentially no geometry. The 54-model archive confirms it: layer_0_pe_h0 spans only [5.50185, 5.59866] (1.8% of its own level) with layer_0_num_features_h0 constant at 49 for every model, and pe_simplification_ratio spans [0.99634, 1.01362]. pe_h1 is the informative column -- archive range [1.44734, 3.70283] with rho(d_model) = +0.006, rho(n_layers) = -0.059, rho(params) = +0.072, rho(vocab) = +0.266 -- so it IS comparable; the shipped headline pe_h0 is not, for a reason that has nothing to do with the implementation. Raising num_samples does not escape the saturation, it only moves the ceiling.
normalized_variant: pe_h0_norm, pe_h1_norm = PE / log2(m), documented in-code as a BLME convenience absent from Atienza et al.
github_repo: GUDHI/gudhi-devel (gudhi.representations.Entropy) and scikit-tda/persim; no code was released with Atienza et al. itself
github_reason: Atienza, Gonzalez-Diaz and Soriano-Trigueros released no code with the paper, but the third author is a GUDHI contributor and `gudhi.representations.Entropy` is the author-linked implementation. I ran GUDHI 3.12.0's Entropy (mode='scalar'), persim 0.3.8's `persistent_entropy` and `scipy.stats.entropy(base=2)` against BLME's `_persistence_entropy` on 300 random diagrams of 2-59 bars: worst absolute differences 2.66e-15, 2.22e-15 and 2.22e-15 respectively (GUDHI and persim use natural log, so their outputs were divided by ln 2). The kernel is also exactly scale-free: over barcode scales 1e-300 to 1e150 the value holds 1.2935343036731686 with a spread of 2.22e-16.
paper_reason: Atienza et al. publish no table value computable from LLM hidden states, so there is no end-to-end published number to reproduce; what the source proves and can be checked exactly is that PE is maximised at log2(m) for m equal-length bars, and BLME reproduces that with error 0.000e+00 at m = 2, 4, 8, 17 and 1000 (1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.087462841250339, 9.965784284662087). Codex's round-5 verdict reports reproducing Chintakunta et al.'s E(F2) = 1.474560793 and E(F3) = 1.459622430 nats to 2.97e-10 / 2.16e-09 by reconstructing the two stated filtrations; I could not fetch that paper (Pattern Recognition, paywalled) to reconstruct them independently, so I record PARTIAL rather than adopting codex's YES on trust. Nothing in my measurements contradicts it -- a kernel that matches GUDHI to 2.66e-15 and the closed form exactly would reproduce any correct published value.
confounds_reason: Neither emitted column is a size proxy on the 54-model archive with resolved HF configs: layer_0_pe_h0 rho(d_model) = -0.169, rho(n_layers) = -0.131, rho(params) = -0.210, rho(vocab) = -0.134; layer_0_pe_h1 rho(d_model) = +0.006, rho(n_layers) = -0.059, rho(params) = +0.072, rho(vocab) = +0.266. The nuisance variable here is the SAMPLE COUNT, not the architecture: pe_h0's bar count is m = N-1 identically for every model (archive layer_0_num_features_h0 = 49 for all 54), which pins pe_h0 to log2(N-1) rather than to any property of the model. Confirmed directly on synthetic clouds: PE/log2(m) = 0.99939-0.99998 across N = 20-400 and D = 64-1024.

CODE persistence_entropy.py:69-70, UNREACHABLE FROM THE SHIPPED PATH but real in the helper: `total = float(arr.sum())` sums before factoring out the maximum, so `_persistence_entropy([1e308, 1e308])` overflows to inf, trips the isfinite guard and returns 0.0 where two equal bars have PE = 1.0 bit exactly (PE([1e300,1e300]) = 1.0 correctly). I checked reachability rather than asserting it: ripser consumes float32, and after the new pre-rescale the cloud's maximum is in [0.707, 1.414], so lifetimes are O(1) and a sum of <= 1000 of them cannot approach float64's limit -- the overflow needs the private helper called with hand-made float64 lifetimes. One-line fix: divide by max(arr) before summing.

CODE persistence_entropy.py:76 `p = p[p > 1e-15]`: the surviving lifetimes are not renormalised after the filter, so `_persistence_entropy([1, 1e-16])` returns 0.0 where the exact value is 5.459354455908675e-15 bits (mpmath at 60 digits). I am NOT treating this as value-changing: the absolute error is 5.5e-15 bits on a statistic whose observed archive range is 1.447-5.599 bits, i.e. below the float64 round-off of the reported value, and the filter fired in 0 of the ordinary barcodes I ran. It is still a one-line renormalisation and should not be left.

CODE persistence_entropy.py:57-59 and 230-232: an EMPTY barcode returns 0.0, which is a legal persistent-entropy value meaning 'one dominant bar' rather than 'no data', and `pe_simplification_ratio` returns 1.0 ('no simplification') when the shallow entropy is 0. Both should be NaN with the bar count reported, as geometry_rsa was corrected in round 4 for mapping an undefined value onto a legal one.

COMPARABILITY defaults.yaml:153-159, num_samples = 1000: pe_h0 saturates at log2(N-1) at every N (PE/log2(m) = 0.99939-0.99998 for N = 20-400), so the 50x forward-pass cost buys a higher ceiling rather than a better statistic -- and at N = 1000 with maxdim = 1 it also buys a Vietoris-Rips H1 computation on 1000 points.

NORMALIZATION persistence_entropy.py:218-219: pe_h0_norm = PE/log2(m) divides by a quantity that is IDENTICAL for every model in a run (m = N-1; archive num_features_h0 = 49 for all 54 models), so it is an exact constant rescale that changes no ranking -- rho(d_model) is -0.169 for both pe_h0 and pe_h0_norm. For H1, where m does vary, it does not remove the association either: rho(vocab) moves +0.266 (pe_h1) to +0.122 while rho(n_layers) moves -0.059 to -0.147, i.e. it relocates rather than removes. It is correctly documented in-code as a BLME convenience.

MINOR: `pe_h0_full` approximates the infinite H0 bar by 2x the maximum finite lifetime. That IS sourced -- Atienza et al. Def. 3.15's projection mu_lambda at lambda = 2, one of the two projections the paper proves stable and scale-invariant -- but the code cites nothing and does not expose lambda.
